reason: Feasible under the feasibility lens; nothing needs building. (1) Code exists and composes: tools/build_probe_kernel.py --patch stitch (stitch_final_graph, STITCH_CAPTURE, STITCH_CALL) and replay.py st.* use the same source text. I applied leafprune+divinsert+edgefilter+stitch+coordhead in memory, in two different patch orders, without writing any repo file. Every cell compiles. The tail order is always leafprune -> linefit -> edgefilter -> stitch -> divinsert, and the ILP capture sits before the motion relink. (2) The kernel cannot crash here. After filter_output_graph the writer reads only source_id/target_id, so the extra 'stitched' key is harmless. The stitch adds about 38 edges per video (6,956 ILP candidates on 199 videos) with O(E) dict work: seconds at most, no GPU and no Kaggle time risk. (3) There is no conflict with existing steps. It runs after relink, gap closing, gap2, safe divisions, the short-track filter, leaf prune, linefit and ef. It adds no nodes (node counts identical in all 135 confirmation videos). The source has out-degree 0, so it cannot create a fork. Candidate ilp_p ranges from 0.480 to 0.9997 (median 0.81), so no stitched edge has p < steal_prob_max 0.3 and DaughterNet steal can never take one. The research's pitfall (3) is therefore moot, and st_all needs no p>=0.6 fallback for that reason. In the kernel, divinsert scores nodes live with DaughterNet (score_nodes on the post-stitch triples), so missing p is only a lab artefact. (4) The lab can run it on a Kaggle CPU kernel or at idle priority. Leaf-prune 0.3 tails already exist (.public_local_cache/l2_replay/l4_leafprune/tail), so the e48 base probably needs no new full tail pass if it reuses that out dir. The contrary claim in the refined lab test is likely wrong. The gate amendment is pure arithmetic on existing per-video CSVs. FEASIBILITY CAVEATS (none fatal): (a) The lab under-measures the stitch x divinsert interaction. The lab node_p set (l2_replay_v2/node_p/21c278c1358028a9) covers only 46% of stitch sources u (the new single-child parent candidates; 62% of candidates are within parent_um 10 um) and 91% of targets v. Triples without p are silently skipped in the lab but scored in the kernel. The effect is capped at 4 insertions per video and is worth at most a few 1e-4 through the 0.1 x division term. (b) The likely final base is exp51 coordhead (float coords, different ILP probs). The lab's fixed integer detector nodes cannot replay it, so stitch-on-coordhead is testable only through the LB bundle. (c) The lab cache used tight gate 6.0 and the kernel uses 5.5, so the candidate set will differ a little (as with ef, about 9.5%). (d) No Kaggle kernel has yet run with STITCH_ENABLE=1. A dummy-clip run's 'stitch: candidates=.. added=..' log line must be checked before submitting, as was done for ef in exp49. (e) The hypothesis's placement 'before the short-track filter and linefit' is wrong and unmeasured. Ship the measured placement after linefit and ef. Its st_p07 form fails the 44b6 mean gate (+0.00078), so ship st_all.
